candidates.label: Movie

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

types.oie_definition: A measure or statistic used in a particular industry, such as box office performance.
types.embedding_query_text: Industry Metric: A measure or statistic used in a particular industry, such as box office performance. Also called statistic, indicator, measure.

chosen_type.label: BoxOfficeMetric
chosen_type.definition: A metric measuring the commercial performance of a film, such as box office revenue.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate fits; 'box office' is a specific industry metric, not a generic statistical variable.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
candidates.comment: An enumeration of methods used for measurement. Also called measurement technique, gauging method, assessment approach. Examples: "manual measurement", "automated sensor measurement", "self-reported measurement".

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: EmployerAggregateRating
candidates.comment: An EmployerAggregateRating is an AggregateRating representing a collective assessment of an Organization's performance as an employer. Also called company rating, employer review score, workplace satisfaction rating. Examples: Glassdoor's overall rating for a company, an average employee satisfaction score, a composite rating from multiple employee surveys.

types.oie_definition: A quantity of money expressed in a specific currency.
types.embedding_query_text: Monetary Amount: A quantity of money expressed in a specific currency. Also called sum of money, amount, figure.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are monetary amounts with currency, fitting MonetaryAmount.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

types.oie_definition: A defined area of the Earth's surface, such as a country or group of countries.
types.embedding_query_text: Geographic Region: A defined area of the Earth's surface, such as a country or group of countries. Also called area, territory, region.

chosen_type.label: AdministrativeArea
chosen_type.justification: 'U.S. and Canada' is a geographic region, best represented by AdministrativeArea.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: MovieRentalStore

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

types.embedding_query_text: Company: A commercial business or organization. Also called business, corporation, firm.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are large companies, fitting Corporation.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A calendar year. Also called calendar year, twelve-month period.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Years are specific dates, fitting the Date datatype.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsTheater
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent

candidates.label: PerformAction

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. candidates.label: Residence

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Date

candidates.label: Event

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: Substance
